record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Comparing success measures in full cognitive-resource-demographic models
record.original_question: For a movement model that simultaneously includes cognitive movement mechanisms, explicit resources, and demographic birth-death processes, how do the different proposed measures of success compare? Do resource-based, demographic, and fitness-style success measures rank strategies consistently, or do they fundamentally disagree about which cognitive strategies are optimal?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 46. For a movement model which includes cognitive movement mechanisms, explicit resources, and birth/death processes, how do various measures of success proposed here compare? Are they consistent with each other, or do they have a fundamental disagreement in which strategies are optimal in each sense of “success”?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a spatially explicit population model on a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ (with suitable boundary conditions) describing an animal population that simultaneously incorporates: (i) cognitive movement mechanisms (e.g., nonlocal perception kernels and/or a dynamic cognitive map $k(x,t)$ representing memory of resource locations, coupled to the population density $u(x,t)$ through advection terms of the form $-\nabla\cdot(u\,\nabla(K*u+\alpha k))$); (ii) an explicit resource field $R(x,t)$ governed by its own dynamics (e.g., logistic growth modulated by consumption: $R_t=g(R)-c(R,u)$); and (iii) demographic birth–death processes acting on $u$ (e.g., $u_t = \dots + f(u,R)$ with $f$ encoding reproduction and mortality dependent on local resources).

For such a coupled system, define and compare the following candidate measures of success of a chosen cognitive strategy $\mathcal{S}$ (parameterized by perception range, memory decay rate, learning rate, etc.) at a stationary or long-time-averaged state:
\begin{itemize}
\item A resource-based measure: e.g., the per-capita resource intake $M_R(\mathcal{S}) = \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T \frac{\int_\Omega c(R,u)\,dx}{\int_\Omega u\,dx}\,dt$.
\item A demographic measure: e.g., the total equilibrium population $M_N(\mathcal{S}) = \lim_{t\to\infty}\int_\Omega u(x,t)\,dx$ or the asymptotic growth rate at low density.
\item A fitness-style measure: e.g., the invasion exponent / principal eigenvalue $M_F(\mathcal{S})$ governing whether a rare mutant strategy $\mathcal{S}'$ can invade a resident population using $\mathcal{S}$.
\end{itemize}

Question: Do these three measures induce the same ordering on the space of admissible cognitive strategies $\mathcal{S}$? Either prove that $M_R$, $M_N$, and $M_F$ are consistent (i.e., they identify the same optimal strategies, possibly under explicit hypotheses on the kernels, resource dynamics, and demographic terms), or exhibit a model within this class for which the rankings fundamentally disagree, so that the strategy optimal in one sense is strictly suboptimal in another.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2022 survey on PDE models of cognitive animal movement. No subsequent works appear to systematically compare resource-based, demographic, and fitness-style success measures for the full coupled cognition–resource–demography model, so the question appears to remain open.
